description: Agent team model agreed 2026-10-24: team labels, A7 updated with roles and the hold rule, A8 agent buttons, A9 vault reports. Applied by the Maintenance workflow (apply-issue-updates).

A7.title: Agent handoff: who works on what
A7.what:
Run the project like a small company, by roles rather than names: any agent can hold any role, and Blake decides who holds which (for example, Codex could coordinate if that works better). **Maintainer** (always Blake): final say, approves merges, decides product questions, the only one who clears a hold, assigns the roles. **Coordinator** (currently Claude, set by the repo variable `COORDINATOR`): writes briefs into issues, assigns them with labels, reviews pull requests and posts a verdict (merge, send back, or Blake's call); never reviews its own pull request. **Builder** (any agent, the coordinator included): takes one issue and one pull request at a time, only from issues labeled `ready` plus its agent label, following the brief in the issue.

Status lives in labels and pull requests that every agent can read and change (the Roadmap board's Status field needs GraphQL, which agents cannot use): `ready`, `agent:claude` / `agent:codex` / `agent:gemini`, `paused` (with a comment saying why; `needs decision` works the same way). In progress = a draft pull request with "Closes #N"; in review = that pull request marked ready.

**Hold rule:** a failed check, a disputed review or an open question puts `hold` on that pull request, and while any open pull request has `hold`, no agent starts new work. Work in progress stays parked. Only Blake removes `hold`. Blake's direct instruction always overrides the labels: an agent told to take another agent's issue takes it and moves the label to itself.
done: The labels exist with short descriptions
AGENTS.md describes the roles (maintainer, coordinator, builder), the one-pull-request-at-a-time rule, the hold rule and Blake's override
The issue health report lists open holds and stale claims (a draft pull request with no activity for a few days)
Tested: an agent refuses to start while a hold exists, and takes another agent's issue when Blake says so

A8.title: Agent buttons: run Claude from anywhere, the team at the Mac
A8.what: An Agents page in the Actions tab so work can be started from GitHub, including from a phone. **Run Claude** runs on GitHub's machines with anthropics/claude-code-action and Blake's subscription token, so it works when the Mac is closed (reviews, tests, labeling, starting builders). **Run Codex** and **Run Gemini** run on Blake's Mac as a GitHub self-hosted runner, using the command-line tools already signed in to his plans (no API keys), so they only work when the Mac is awake. Every button obeys A7's hold rule. Buttons only: no comment-triggered runs, because anyone can comment on a public repo.
done: Run Claude works with the Mac closed and posts its result on the issue or pull request
Run Codex and Run Gemini work on the Mac runner and open a draft pull request for their next ready issue
Fork pull requests can't run anything on the Mac: the repo requires approval for outside contributors' workflows and only button-started jobs use the Mac runner
Every button stops when a hold exists
Tested with one agent end to end before adding the others

A9.title: Reports for the note vault
A9.what: Write the project's GitHub activity as Markdown notes on a `reports` branch, which Blake's note vault pulls with git (Obsidian git plugin). One note per merged pull request: date, issue, milestone, its plain-words description, Tested / Not tested, every check result including failures with their dates, and its screenshot embedded. The weekly update is also written as a note that links to that week's pull request notes, so backlinks connect them. Notes are compiled from the pull requests' own words, never written by AI. Properties at the top of each note so Obsidian, SiYuan or VaultOps can sort and filter. Screenshot cleanup only deletes a screenshot after its report note has a copy. This is a live test of VaultOps' own repo-link idea.
done: Merging a pull request adds its note (with the screenshot) to the reports branch
The weekly update also lands as a note linking that week's pull request notes
Screenshot cleanup skips screenshots that are not yet copied into a report
Tested by pulling the reports branch into a test vault and checking links and images

ready.description: Has a brief and can be picked up

hold.description: Problem or open question: no agent starts new work until Blake clears it

paused.description: Parked on purpose; a comment says why
